source_branches.when: bulk add, reactivation, workspace-role caps, and invite effects
source_branches.observable: members defaults to []; empty list returns 400. Every requested user must have active workspace membership. Workspace ADMIN cannot grant project MEMBER/GUEST; workspace GUEST cannot grant ADMIN/MEMBER; workspace MEMBER has no role cap. Duplicate IDs collapse in role map with last role winning. Existing rows, including inactive rows, are reactivated and role-updated; new memberships and ProjectUserProperty rows use bulk_create/ignore_conflicts. Enqueues project_add_user_email per resulting row. Returns HTTP 201 with an array of ProjectMemberRoleSerializer rows: {id, member, role, project, original_role, created_at}. The source runtime fixture confirms this exact shape. Duplicate IDs collapse in the role map with the last role winning, while the original submitted list can still contribute inserts.

Ordinary OPTIONS is handled by DRF metadata and returns 200 with POST actions for ProjectMemberAdminSerializer. An invalid timezone returns 400 before metadata dispatch. Collection HEAD belongs to the previously retired GET path and is excluded from this family replay; the production proxy preserves its existing Go behavior.
A new membership with omitted role is created with role 5.
A new project property uses the existing workspace/user minimum sort_order minus 10000.
A workspace MEMBER may be assigned project ADMIN by the authorized requester.

source_branches.when: bulk request shape, role coercion, and row updates
source_branches.observable: JSON null and JSON list request bodies each return 500 with the generic error and no recorded database delta. A guest-target role supplied as numeric 20 is rejected with 400, but string "20" passes the source role-cap membership check, is database-coerced to role 20, returns 201, and emits the invite task. A mixed batch with an inactive existing member and a later non-integer role returns 500 after the existing row is reactivated; no invite task is emitted.

source_branches.when: stored role values outside declared choices
source_branches.observable: An authorized project administrator can bulk-create a workspace MEMBER with integer role 10; the source bulk insert stores the value without model choice validation and returns it in the create representation. Later authorized list/lite/PATCH responses preserve stored role 10.

A missing or null member_id, boolean true, numeric 123, or a syntactically valid but nonexistent workspace member return 404. JSON list/object member_id values return 500 with the generic error. These outcomes follow ORM UUID preparation and lookup rather than serializer choice validation.

source_branches.when: role, active-state, and serializer field authorization
source_branches.observable: Requester and target need active project memberships. Self-update is rejected except workspace admin. Non-workspace-admin role change requires project ADMIN; cannot alter equal/higher target role or assign equal/higher role; guest targets cannot be raised above guest. is_active uses its independent hierarchy guard. App serializer exposes all model fields except read-only workspace/project/member; deleted_at remains writable. Empty patch succeeds and saves updated_at/updated_by while preserving membership fields.

A JSON null PATCH body returns 500 with the generic error before serializer validation. An invalid UUID for updated_by returns 400 with a UUID validation error; a syntactically valid but missing user UUID returns 400 with an invalid primary-key error. Neither rejected updated_by request changes membership state.

Legacy PATCH requires an active project membership with declared role ADMIN, MEMBER, or GUEST, or the source workspace-admin override with active project membership. An active role-10 project member receives 403; making that same workspace member ADMIN restores access through the override. Role 10 remains reachable through legacy bulk creation and is a response value, not an authorization role.

known_source_security_limitation: Legacy PATCH serializer includes writable deleted_at. Source fixtures prove lower-role project members and guests can set it on a higher-role membership without invoking the soft-delete cascade. Preserve the measured source behavior for parity; authorization hardening is a separate product change.
protocol_companion_policy: API-key HEAD and ordinary OPTIONS return source 405 after method-specific authorization and timezone checks. The lite route additionally records unsupported PATCH and POST: permission checks are method-specific before its 405 dispatch. Legacy leave HEAD returns 405; legacy collection/detail GET and HEAD already belong to the retired read family and preserve its production behavior, verified by baseline/candidate proxy differential. Raw Django collection/detail HEAD no longer represents their live contract and is excluded from this family replay. Legacy ordinary OPTIONS returns 200 DRF metadata for collection, detail, and leave; collection/leave include POST action metadata and detail has no write-action metadata. Legacy collection OPTIONS with invalid timezone returns 400 before metadata dispatch. CORS preflight is a shared middleware response. New protocol fixtures are attached to matching GET operations where present; write-only protocol evidence remains in shared_protocol_fixture_refs.

differential_replay.environment: Compare baseline and candidate production proxies with equivalent isolated seeds. The baseline proxy preserves already-retired legacy membership GETs; selected writes still route to immutable source Django. Detail samples use a missing membership and leave uses the sole administrator, so the method matrix preserves seed state; successful write effects are proven by source-fixture replay.
